findings.issue: q7 shifts the stated pinch-cover responsibility from F3 to D2 without a scene change.
findings.evidence: The briefing says YOU may pinch only while F3 covers the high position; q7 instead keys the call to D2, whose position is low and whose cover is not declared.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace q7 with: What should YOU communicate before stepping down? Options: (a) F3 is the high cover only while the lane stays connected; (b) The pinch has already won the puck; (c) Gold 1 no longer affects the decision. Answer [a]. Explanation: F3 is the named cover in this drill, but the puck route and recovery lane still need checking. Rehash q7.

findings.issue: q7 treats a D1 call on Gold 2 as an established event, but the scene only states that D1 is set to contain Gold 1.
findings.evidence: The briefing assigns D1 to the wide Gold 1 route; it does not say D1 called Gold 2. q7 asks what to say after that unstated call and keys a new assignment.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace q7 with: What should YOU communicate while D1 contains Gold 1? Options: (a) I have Gold 2; call if Gold 1 cuts inside; (b) The puck is already safe; (c) D1 will cover both attackers. Answer [a]. Explanation: Name your Gold 2 responsibility and the condition that would change the handoff; D1’s stated carrier call remains visible. Rehash q7.

findings.issue: q10 asks the child to decide whether D1 or YOU takes the new relationship, but no D1 actor exists in the scene.
findings.evidence: The setup contains YOU, D2, C, Gold 1–3 and G; the briefing names the low exchange with D2 and slot cover by C, never D1.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace D1 in q10 with D2, or add a clearly positioned D1 and state that role in the briefing. Keep the side exchange and slot responsibility consistent, then rehash q10.

findings.issue: q9’s reference moves YOU away from the Navy net while the prompt says to move closer than the wall battle.
findings.evidence: The battle is at x=-11 and YOU starts at x=-5; q9 reference x=-4 moves toward Gold’s end (+x), not closer to Navy’s net (-x).
findings.recommendedChange: Change q9 reference to a more negative x such as {x:-13,y:3.2}, or rewrite the prompt/explanation to describe an attacking-side support pocket. Recheck separation from F1 and visibility of C, then rehash q9.

findings.issue: q4 claims to open a diagonal lane to F3, but its reference barely moves YOU and remains on the upper wall rather than illustrating a meaningful line toward F3.
findings.evidence: YOU starts at (18,9), F3 is at (21,-1), and the reference is (19.5,8.1); the direct line toward F3 is substantially lower, so the stated diagonal change is not represented.
findings.recommendedChange: Move the reference into a clearly different angle toward F3, for example {x:19.5,y:4}, while checking it does not collide with Gold 1 or F2; or change the prompt to a small half-wall angle adjustment. Rehash q4.

findings.issue: q7 changes the explicit 48-second situation to one minute left.
findings.evidence: The briefing states Navy leads by one with 48 seconds remaining; q7 asks “with one minute left,” which is a different game state and can change the risk read.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace q7 prompt with “What should YOU communicate with 48 seconds left?” Keep the conditional option and explanation, or say “under a minute” if exact precision is not intended. Rehash q7.

findings.issue: q7 and q8 refer to D1 as the deeper cover, but the scene explicitly assigns that role to D2.
findings.evidence: The briefing says D2 stays deeper by agreement. q7 says “D1 is behind me,” and q8 asks whether D1 leaves the deeper cover; D1 is not the assigned cover in this setup.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace D1 with D2 in q7 and q8, preserving the rest of each question: q7 “F1 has control and D2 is behind me; call if either changes”; q8 option b “D2 leaves the deeper cover.” Rehash q7/q8.

findings.issue: q9 says to move toward D1’s vacated point, but its reference remains near F1 behind the net rather than the point area.
findings.evidence: D1’s current point is (23,7), while q9 reference is (20,1), close to F1 at (28,0) and not a high-point illustration.
findings.recommendedChange: Change q9 reference to a high point such as {x:21,y:6}, while keeping F1 visible, or rewrite the prompt to describe a low support angle. Recheck separation and rehash q9.

scenarios.title: Pinch only with the declared cover
scenarios.objective: Evaluate a pinch under an explicitly stated cover assignment.
scenarios.briefing: Navy uses a drill rule: YOU may pinch the puck-side wall only while F3 covers your high position. F1 contests Gold 1’s rim; F3 is currently closer to Gold’s net than the puck, so the named cover is not established. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: F3 is deeper in the attacking zone than YOU, rather than occupying the high position.

questions.prompt: Is the stated high cover already established?

options.text: Yes; F3 has replaced YOU at the point
Yes; Gold 2 is Navy’s cover
No; F3 is currently closer to Gold’s net than YOU

questions.explanation: F3 is deeper in the attacking zone than YOU, rather than occupying the high position.

questions.prompt: Select two checks before acting on the pinch option.

options.text: Whether F3 can establish the agreed cover
The quality of the puck contest
Whether a rim always requires a pinch

questions.explanation: The source principle is conditional support; this exercise adds its own explicit cover rule.

questions.prompt: Arrange a supported-pinch decision.

options.text: Read the wall contest
Confirm the assigned high cover
Pinch or recover based on the updated picture

questions.explanation: The checks may overlap. Do not treat this drill’s cover rule as every team’s system.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a conservative high position while cover is uncertain.
questions.explanation: The reference retains access to central recovery rather than committing to the wall. Other high positions may work.

questions.prompt: F3 now reaches your vacated point and calls the switch. What changes?

options.text: The cover condition is met, but the puck contest still needs checking
The pinch becomes certain to win
Gold 1 no longer affects the decision

questions.explanation: A covered pinch can still lose a race or encounter a closed route.

questions.prompt: Explain what makes this a supported pinch rather than simply an aggressive move.
questions.explanation: Identify F3’s actual coverage, D2’s position and the puck situation; do not rely on the word “pinch” alone.

questions.prompt: F3 has not reached YOUR high position. Which call fits before a possible pinch?

options.text: F3, confirm high cover before I step down
D2 is on the ice, so I am going now
F1 is near the puck, so the cover can wait

questions.explanation: The drill names F3 as the replacement for YOUR high position. Ask for that cover and check the puck route before committing; a call alone does not establish it.

questions.prompt: After F3 reaches high cover, which changes would make YOU reconsider the pinch?

options.text: F3 leaves that high position
The puck moves beyond F1’s reachable route
Gold stays away from the puck

questions.explanation: The hypothetical cover is now established, but a change in cover or puck access can remove the reason to pinch. Hold or recover if the updated picture no longer supports it.

questions.prompt: Move F3 to illustrate the named replacement for YOUR high position.
questions.explanation: F3 is now near YOUR high area, on the neutral-zone side of the wall contest. This illustrates the cover condition; whether a pinch is reachable still needs a fresh puck read.

questions.prompt: F3 reaches YOUR high area, but the loose puck travels past F1 toward neutral ice. What changes?
questions.explanation: High cover satisfies only one condition. If YOU cannot reach the puck safely, hold or recover and communicate the escape route. F3 arriving does not make every pinch useful.

scenarios.objective: Coordinate recovering help rather than duplicate wide pressure.

In this drill D1 calls that the carrier is covered. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.

A belief that D2 can cover every possible turnover alone
Whether to hold or recover instead of continuing up ice

The attack makes cover unnecessary

scenarios.title: A defender rotates low while a forward covers the point
scenarios.objective: Understand a declared role exchange without confusing jersey position with current responsibility.
scenarios.briefing: F1 controls behind the Gold net. D1 has rotated low on one side. YOU are F3 and the coach has explicitly assigned YOU to cover D1’s vacated point until the exchange ends. D2 remains at the opposite point. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
